content: Possible Side Effects In the United States, if you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions Before starting pyrazinamide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid alcohol consumption while taking this medication, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Pyrazinamide may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as determined by your doctor. Pyrazinamide can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Pyrazinamide may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine ketone tests, potentially leading to false results. Overdose If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Laboratory and Medical Monitoring While taking this medication, your doctor may order regular laboratory tests, such as sputum tests, kidney and liver function tests, uric acid levels, and complete blood counts, to monitor your condition and the medication's effects. Be sure to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose It is important to take each dose of this medication as prescribed. If you are taking this medication daily and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. If you are on a weekly dosing schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day or later, contact your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. Storage Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. Important Information This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses Pyrazinamide is used in combination with other medications to treat tuberculosis (TB). This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. If you are taking it daily, take it at the same time each day. If you are on a weekly schedule, take it on the same day(s) of the week and at the same time. Continue taking this medication, along with other TB medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. Side Effects Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or mild muscle or joint pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor.
